newsitem.title: MEXICO: Do homework before backing VAT cuts -Mexico's Orti.
newsitem.headline: Do homework before backing VAT cuts -Mexico's Orti.

text.p: Opposition parties proposing to slash Mexico's value added tax (VAT) by five percent have not done their homework properly, Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz was quoted on Saturday as saying.

Ortiz was stepping into a debate over VAT that has heated up since opposition parties made exceptional gains in mid-term elections earlier this month. They want to make good campaign promises to reduce the unpopular tax to 10 percent from 15.
But Mexico's Reforma newspaper quoted Ortiz as saying that the proposals had not been properly thought out and would cost the country billions of pesos.

"I am very respectful of the parties' proposals and I know that the function of the government is to analyse them, discuss them and consider their viability, but I consider that this is an incomplete proposal," he said.

"How should we compensate for this (cutting VAT)," he asked. "Will we raise other taxes in order to reduce spending? In what area, cuts to education, to health?" he said, adding he hopes the proposals would take Mexico's whole economic picture into account.
Instead he favoured studying other measures that would improve business and family accounts, including cutting tax on rents, the paper said.

"What is fundamental for the country, for its stability and economic development, is to maintain healthy public finances that are close to being balanced, in such a way that if people make demands to reduce the level of VAT they have to realise the fiscal cost would be close to 24 billion pesos ($3.04 billion) in 1996," he said.
